# 1 Kings Chapter 10 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-the-queen-of Sheba heard ʾet-the-report-of Solomon concerning-the-name-of YHWH, and-she-came to-test-him with-riddles.

**2** And-she-came to-Jerusalem with-a-very great retinue — camels carrying spices and-gold in-great-abundance and-precious stones. And-she-came to Solomon and-spoke to-him ʾet-all that was on her-heart.

**3** And-Solomon told-her ʾet-all her-words; there-was-not a-thing hidden from the-king that he-did-not tell-her.

**4** And-the-queen-of Sheba saw ʾet-all the-wisdom-of Solomon and-the-house that he-built,

**5** and-the-food-of his-table and-the-seating-of his-servants and-the-standing-of his-attendants and-their-clothing and-his-cupbearers, and-his-burnt-offering that he-offered at-the-house-of YHWH — and-there-was no more spirit in-her.

**6** And-she-said to the-king, "True was the-word that I-heard in-my-land concerning your-words and-concerning your-wisdom.

**7** And-I-did-not believe the-words until I-came and-my-eyes saw — and-behold, the-half was-not told to-me. You-have-added wisdom and-good beyond the-report that I-heard.

**8** Happy are your-men; happy are these your-servants who-stand before-you continually, who-hear ʾet-your-wisdom.

**9** Blessed is YHWH your-God, who delighted in-you, to-set-you on the-throne-of Israel. Because-of-the-love-of YHWH for-Israel forever, he-made-you king, to-do justice and-righteousness."

**10** And-she-gave to-the-king a-hundred and-twenty talents-of gold and-spices in-very-great abundance, and-precious stones. There-never came again such abundance-of spices as-that which the-queen-of Sheba gave to-the-king Solomon.

**11** And-also the-fleet-of Hiram that carried gold from-Ophir brought from-Ophir almug wood in-great-abundance and-precious stones.

**12** And-the-king made from-the-almug wood supports for-the-house-of YHWH and-for-the-house-of the-king, and-lyres and-harps for-the-singers. Such almug wood has-not come nor-been-seen to this day.

**13** And-the-king Solomon gave to-the-queen-of Sheba ʾet-all her-desire, that she-asked, besides what he-gave-her according-to-the-hand-of the-king Solomon. And-she-turned and-went to-her-land — she and-her-servants.

**14** And-the-weight-of the-gold that came to-Solomon in-one year was six-hundred and-sixty-six talents-of gold,

**15** besides that from the-men-of the-traders and-the-profit-of the-merchants and-all the-kings-of the-mixed-peoples and-the-governors-of the-land.

**16** And-the-king Solomon made two-hundred large-shields-of beaten gold — six-hundred shekels-of gold went on each large-shield.

**17** And-three-hundred shields-of beaten gold — three minas-of gold went on each shield. And-the-king put-them in-the-House-of the-Forest-of Lebanon.

**18** And-the-king made a-great throne-of ivory, and-overlaid-it with-refined gold.

**19** Six steps had-the-throne, and-a-round-top to-the-throne from-behind-it, and-armrests on-each-side by-the-place-of sitting, and-two lions standing beside the-armrests.

**20** And-twelve lions standing there on the-six steps, on-each-side. Nothing like-it was-made for-any kingdom.

**21** And-all the-drinking-vessels-of the-king Solomon were-of gold, and-all the-vessels-of the-House-of the-Forest-of Lebanon were-of refined gold. None were-of silver — it-was-not reckoned as-anything in-the-days-of Solomon.

**22** For a-fleet-of Tarshish the-king had at-sea with the-fleet-of Hiram. Once in-three years the-fleet-of Tarshish would-come, carrying gold and-silver, ivory, and-apes and-peacocks.

**23** And-the-king Solomon was-greater than-all the-kings-of the-earth in-riches and-in-wisdom.

**24** And-all the-earth was-seeking ʾet-the-face-of Solomon, to-hear ʾet-his-wisdom that God had-put in-his-heart.

**25** And-they — each-one bringing his-gift: vessels-of silver and-vessels-of gold, and-garments, and-armor, and-spices, horses and-mules — the-matter-of each-year in-its-year.

**26** And-Solomon gathered chariots and-horsemen. And-he-had a-thousand and-four-hundred chariots and-twelve-thousand horsemen. And-he-placed-them in-the-chariot-cities and-with the-king in-Jerusalem.

**27** And-the-king made ʾet-the-silver in-Jerusalem as-stones, and-ʾet-the-cedars he-made as-the-sycamores that are in-the-Shephelah, in-abundance.

**28** And-the-export-of horses that Solomon had was from-Egypt and-from-Kue — the-traders-of the-king would-take-them from-Kue at-a-price.

**29** And-a-chariot came-up and-went-out from-Egypt for-six-hundred shekels-of silver, and-a-horse for-a-hundred and-fifty. And-so for-all the-kings-of the-Hittites and-the-kings-of Aram — by-their-hand they-exported.

---
## EMET Textual Notes

1. **10:1 — "concerning-the-name-of YHWH"**: The queen comes because of Solomon's fame connected to YHWH — the temple has achieved its purpose of making God's name known internationally.

2. **10:5 — "no more spirit in-her"**: Hebrew lo hayah vah ʿod ruaḥ — she was breathless, overwhelmed. The same expression used for shock or awe elsewhere.

3. **10:14 — "six-hundred and-sixty-six talents"**: This number will resonate in later apocalyptic literature (Rev 13:18). Whether the echo is intentional or coincidental, the number represents the apex of human wealth-accumulation.

4. **10:22 — "apes and-peacocks"**: Hebrew qophim ve-tukkiyim. The exotic cargo list demonstrates the global reach of Solomon's trade network and its luxury orientation.

5. **10:26-29 — horses from Egypt**: Each detail violates Deuteronomy 17:16: "He shall not multiply horses for himself, nor cause the people to return to Egypt to multiply horses." Solomon's horse trade with Egypt directly contravenes the king-law.

— EMET
